text:
sara: FYI customer Keystone (dedicated pool) opened a sev2 — after a traffic spike their endpoints saw long tail 503/timeout and the dedicated pool didn’t scale up fast enough. Ticket #K-9821. Can we triage? :warning:
kevin: Timeline from customer: spike at 09:02, 9:05-9:12 repeated 429s then 503s, requests queued >10s. They say nodes showed new pods but requests still failed.
autoscale-bot: [alert] autoscaler: scale request at 2025-06-15T09:03Z -> desired=18 current=3 minReplicas=1 maxReplicas=100 step=+3 (rateLimit=1/s)
jia: Can you grab pod statuses & the init logs for the new pods? My hunch: readiness blocked (init container or post-start hook).
sara: grabbing logs from the dedicated cluster now — short snippets below.
```
kubectl get pods -n customer-keystone
NAME                                   READY  STATUS      RESTARTS   AGE
app-5b6c8d9f7f-zz1p                   0/2    Init:0/1     0          2m
app-5b6c8d9f7f-qp9t                   1/2    Running      0          30s
```
and init log from app-5b6c8d9f7f-zz1p:
```
> running post-install: pip install -r /app/requirements.txt
Collecting heavy-lib
Downloading from registry... 429 Too Many Requests
retrying...
Still downloading, sleeping 5s
```
jia: yep that's it — init container doing network installs. init must finish before the pod is Ready (so autoscaler only counts once ready). If registry is throttling, that adds tens of seconds per pod.
omar: also saw registry errors in node kubelet logs earlier: `ERR image pull: received 429 from registry` — noisy neighbor on the pool was pulling lots of large images at the same time which hit docker hub rate limits for that node IP range.
kevin: is that a config/scale policy issue or an infra problem? Customer is asking why autoscaler didn't spin up enough capacity fast enough.
jia: multiple factors combined:
- minReplicas=1 so warm capacity minimal
- scale step limited (controller only adds 3 pods/sec due to cooldown/rateLimit)
- init hooks add ~30-60s per pod when pip hits registry 429s
So effective ramp << traffic growth.
sara: repro steps I used in staging (to simulate):
```
# heavy ramp to mimic customer spike
wrk -t4 -c200 -d60s http://dedicated-keystone.myredwood/api/predict
```
I could reproduce increased latencies when init work executed on new pods. Staging didn't have registry throttling so milder but still visible.
jia: fixes (short/long term):
- short: bump minReplicas to 4-6 for this customer or temporarily increase reserved capacity, or enable image pre-pull (DaemonSet) to reduce pull/init time. Also set a faster prewarm policy for this route.
- short (quick toggle): patch deployment to skip init step via env `NO_INIT=1` (safe if using baked image) or set `imagePullPolicy: IfNotPresent` and ensure images are pre-pulled.
- long: bake dependencies into the image (move pip install to image build), remove network installs from init. Also consider autoscaler config: raise burst limit and reduce stabilization window for this pool.
omar: operational note: raising minReplicas will increase host/hour billing — flag to CS before changes. Prepull can be done with a small DaemonSet that pulls image on each node — low cost and quick.
kevin: customer accepts temporary bump to minReplicas but wants to avoid long bill shock. Can we do a 2-hour bump and pre-pull?
sara: I'll propose minReplicas=5 for 2h + deploy a pre-pull DaemonSet. If that stops 503s we'll schedule an image bake next week. Assigning to @jia and @omar to run the change and validate. :thumbsup: 
jia: I'll patch minReplicas and create a DaemonSet; will post the commands and link to the rollout logs here.
omar: also opened a small runbook note to add to the Dedicated troubleshooting docs about "init-hook blocking scale" and registry throttles.
sara: thanks — I'll update Keystone and close the loop when we confirm.
```
